result.rule: Use an exclusive merge for alternative paths; it does not wait for inactive alternatives.
Use an inclusive split when one or more conditions can be true; use an inclusive join to synchronize only activated reachable branches.
Use gateways to control divergence and convergence, never to represent work. Identify exclusive, inclusive, parallel, event-driven or complex behavior.
Several unconditional outgoing flows from one activity can all proceed. Use a gateway when the description requires a decision or synchronization.
Use a parallel join when a shared continuation waits for all active parallel branches. Never use it to join mutually exclusive alternatives.
Use a parallel split when all outgoing branches start. Do not add decision conditions to parallel branches.

result.rule: Distinguish message tasks from message events: a task models performed work; an event models a message occurrence affecting flow.
Do not merge separately described actions into one task or split one stated action without a process reason. Preserve described dependencies.
Model every distinct activity, event, participant, decision, branch, loop, message and outcome stated in the description. Do not invent process facts.
Do not create separate pools for ordinary internal roles unless the description treats them as independent communicating participants.
Do not infer a task subtype only from a verb in its label; require supporting meaning in the full description.
A white-box participant references its process with processRef. A black-box participant has no processRef and no modeled internal workflow.

result.rule: When the description distinguishes initiating or submitting a request from registering it before a later participant receives or handles it: model the initiation or submission and registration as separate activities, preserving their stated order before routing the request onward

When the description states that a distinct activity occurs between a preceding process stage and a later activity: Model the activity as a separate task and connect it to the preceding and following flow in the stated order.

When the description states distinct activities in sequence and indicates that later work may be repeated or changed in response to earlier results, without naming a separate activity for communicating those results.: Model the stated activities in order, represent repetition with a decision and return flow, and treat results as information unless a distinct communication activity is explicitly stated.
When the description distinguishes receiving proposals or offers from choosing among them: Model the choice as a separate activity rather than treating receipt of a proposal or offer as the choice.
